supplementalWages.paidWithRegularWages: Combine and treat as one regular-period payment.
supplementalWages.separateWithoutRegularWithholding: Add to regular wages for the current or preceding payroll period in the same calendar year and compute as one payment.
supplementalWages.separateWithRegularWithholding: Aggregate with current or preceding regular wages, calculate combined withholding, then subtract withholding already taken from regular wages.
supplementalWages.substantialOverwithholdingAlternative: Use the percentage corresponding to the highest bracket expected on the employee's annual Mississippi return.

residencyAndWorkRules.residentRule: Mississippi residents are taxable on all wages, including work outside Mississippi; when the work state requires withholding, the employer should withhold that state's tax rather than Mississippi tax and the resident may claim the allowed return credit.
residencyAndWorkRules.nonresidentRule: Withhold on wages for services performed in Mississippi, subject to the published annual standard-deduction de minimis.
residencyAndWorkRules.nonresidentAnnualDeMinimis: No withholding when expected annual Mississippi earnings are less than the standard deduction for the filing status.

partlyInsideAndOutsideAllocation.principalPlaceInMississippiException: When the principal place of employment is in Mississippi and out-of-state services are occasional, withhold on total wages unless the other state requires withholding.

certificateAdministration.submitToDepartmentWhen: More than 10 allowances are claimed, or exempt is claimed and normal wages exceed $200 per week.

filing.monthly: Average withholding liability of $300 or more per month, and transient or seasonal employers
filing.quarterly: Smaller liabilities unless the Department assigns another frequency
filing.returnDue: 15th day of the month following the reporting period
